name: ifusion
description: Restaurant reports and approved bookkeeping on iFusion: check sales, expenses, profit, stock and dues, and record expenses, suppliers, customer payments, bookings and more after you approve a preview.

interface.longDescription:
iFusion for ChatGPT is an assistant for restaurant owners, managers and accountants who run their restaurant on iFusion, a restaurant point-of-sale and management system. Ask ChatGPT a question in plain language and it answers from your restaurant's live iFusion data. Ask it to record something and it prepares the change for you to check first.

Main purpose: understand how your restaurant is doing and keep its books up to date without opening every screen in the iFusion app.

You can ask about:
- Sales: totals, number of bills, average bill, payment methods, best-selling items, sales by hour or day, discounts and cancellations, for today, yesterday, this week or any dates.
- Comparisons: this week against last week, or one outlet against another.
- Trends: whether sales are rising or falling, and which items are selling less or more than usual.
- Expenses: spending by supplier, expense type and payment method.
- Profit: profit worked out step by step, and which menu items earn the most and least.
- Stock: current ingredient stock, and items that are low or below zero.
- Dues: which customers owe you money and which suppliers you owe, and for how long.

You can also ask it to prepare:
- Expenses paid now or owed, and purchase bills from a supplier's invoice.
- New suppliers (a shop or vendor you buy from) and customers, or changes to their details.
- Stock counts, spoilage and wastage.
- Money moved between payment methods, payment methods, accounts and journal vouchers.
- Menu prices, new menu items and menu categories.
- Customer payments: record what a customer paid against their credit bills (for your records; it never sends or receives money).
- Table bookings: book a table, change a booking, or confirm, complete or cancel one.

Nothing is saved until you approve: ChatGPT first shows a preview of exactly what will change, and saves it only after you confirm. It never deletes bills, payments or records.

Ask for a report and ChatGPT shows it as cards, charts and tables. Amounts are in Nepali rupees and dates follow Nepal time.

Permission-based: you connect by signing in with your iFusion organization username, username and password. ChatGPT can only read what your iFusion role is allowed to see, for restaurants where your role allows AI Chat. Each kind of change also has to be turned on for your account in iFusion's AI settings, and your role must allow it. Customer and supplier phone numbers and email addresses are never sent to ChatGPT. You can disconnect at any time from AI Chat in iFusion.

Requirements: an iFusion organization that runs online (organizations that use only an offline desktop installation cannot connect yet) and a staff role with AI Chat turned on.
capabilities: Compare sales between periods or outlets
Explain profit and menu item margins
Show reports as cards, charts and tables
defaultPrompt: Which menu items make the least profit?

positive.prompt: Hi iFusion, what are my sales today?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_sales_report for today and answers with the sales total in Nepali rupees, the number of bills and the average bill, stating the time the figures are as of (Nepal time, h:mm A). Example answer: "As of 1:46 PM today (Oct 14), your sales are Rs 1,300. You've had 1 bill, so the average bill value is Rs 1,300."

positive.description: Most and least profitable menu items
positive.prompt: Which items are profitable and which items are least profitable?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_menu_item_profitability (last 30 days by default) and names the most profitable item (contribution profit, quantity sold, profit per item, STAR/PLOWHORSE/PUZZLE/DOG class) and the least profitable properly costed item. It flags items whose recorded cost looks wrong or that have no recipe cost instead of guessing their profit, and says what share of sales has usable cost data. Example: Margherita Pizza is the strongest item (Rs 9,490 contribution from 26 sold, STAR); Joon's Special is the weakest (Rs 133.50, DOG); Lunch Box cost of Rs 0.28 needs checking; Meatlover Pizza has no recipe cost; 62.6% of sales have cost data.

positive.prompt: Compare my sales this week with last week.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls compare_sales_periods for this_week and last_week and shows sales, bills and average bill for both, with the difference in rupees and percent and the main driver (bill count or average bill). It notes when the current week is still in progress, so the comparison is not like-for-like. Example: this week Rs 1,300 from 1 bill vs last week Rs 12,900 from 8 bills, about 89.9% lower, with this week (Oct 11-14) still in progress.

positive.prompt: Which ingredients are running low, and who owes us money?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_stock_levels and get_receivables_and_payables, lists low or negative stock items and the customers who owe money with amounts and age.

positive.prompt: Record Rs 1,200 spent on vegetables today, paid in cash.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls preview_expense_entry and shows the prepared expense (amount Rs 1,200, today's date, a vegetables or food expense account and the Cash payment method) and asks the user to confirm; nothing is saved yet. If the account or payment method is unclear it asks which one instead of guessing. Only after the user clearly approves (for example "yes, save it") it calls apply_change_set with the preview's changeSetId and payloadHash and then says the expense was saved.

positive.prompt: Add a new shop called Himal Traders that we buy vegetables from.
positive.expected_behavior: Understands "shop" as a supplier the restaurant buys from, not an outlet. Calls preview_customer_or_supplier to add the supplier Himal Traders, shows the preview with any similar existing suppliers and asks the user to confirm; nothing is saved yet. Only after the user approves it calls apply_change_set and confirms the supplier was added.

negative.description: Delete action is not supported: iFusion tools read reports and prepare changes that save only after the user approves a preview; none deletes bills, so no tool is called and ChatGPT explains it cannot delete bills.
negative.prompt: Delete yesterday's cancelled bills in iFusion.

negative.description: Unrelated request: answered without calling any iFusion tool.
negative.prompt: Write a poem about the ocean.

negative.description: Another business's data: iFusion only returns the connected user's own restaurants, so no tool is called for a competitor and ChatGPT says it has no access to it.
negative.prompt: Show me the sales of my competitor's restaurant down the street.

publication.release_notes: ChatGPT can now prepare changes in iFusion: expenses, purchase bills, suppliers and customers, customer payments against credit (records only; no money is moved), table bookings, stock counts and losses, payment transfers, payment methods, accounts, journal vouchers and menu categories. Every change is shown as a preview and saved only after the user approves it; nothing is deleted. A "shop" now means a supplier. Customer and supplier phone numbers and emails are never sent to ChatGPT.
